# Architecture

## Two things in one repository

- **The package.** `npx tinyfactory <name>` (`bin/tinyfactory.mjs`) runs the bootstrap skill, which sets up a new project: a repository, a board, the factory, an app, hosting and a database.
- **The factory.** Skills, workflows, scripts and their tests. It is copied into every project, and it also runs here, to build tinyfactory.

There is no app in this repository. A change here is a change to the factory or to the package.

## Where things are

| Folder | Holds |
|---|---|
| `bin/` | The command a person runs |
| `.claude/skills/` | One skill for each agent's job. `bootstrap/` is setup: its scripts, the manifest and the templates |
| `.claude/skills/bootstrap/templates/` | What a new project starts with and tinyfactory does not use itself: seed documents, and the app's lint and test setup |
| `factory/workflows/` | The source of every workflow |
| `.github/workflows/` | The copies GitHub runs, installed from the sources after a merge. Never edited |
| `factory/scripts/` | What the workflows run. Bash, each with its use in its first lines |
| `factory/tests/` | A test file for each script; `helpers.sh` makes the stand-ins for outside commands |
| `factory/decisions/`, `factory/free-tier/` | The records: one file for each ticket |
| `product/` | What users of tinyfactory said, and product decisions |

## What reaches a project

Setup copies two things into a new project, and nothing else:

- **The paths in `.claude/skills/bootstrap/manifest.txt`.** The factory owns them, and they are the same in every project.
- **The templates.** Each project edits its copies afterwards.

Everything at the root of this repository (`PURPOSE.md`, this file, `TASTE.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `package.json`, `product/`) is tinyfactory's own and reaches no project. The copy is one-way and happens once: a project owns its files from then on.

So a change to a file in the manifest changes every project set up afterwards. What only this repository needs is kept out of a project by name, where the script that copies decides (`scaffold.sh`).

## Principles

- **A script before an agent.** What a script or a check can decide, it decides. An agent is for judgement.
- **One workflow for each event, one skill for each job.** A workflow runs an agent with one skill when its event arrives.
- **A workflow never runs before it is reviewed.** It is changed in `factory/workflows/`, where GitHub runs nothing, and installed once its pull request has merged.
- **Only the owner starts anything.** A workflow that runs an agent, holds a secret or writes to the repository acts for the repository's owner and for nobody else.
- **Every script has a test.** The test stands in for each outside command and proves each failure as well as the success.

## Domain language

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Project | A repository that `npx tinyfactory` set up |
| Owner | The GitHub account that owns the repository |
| Ticket | A GitHub issue written to a template. The `ready` label starts its build |
| Manifest | The list of paths the factory owns in every project |
| Seed | A template a project edits after setup |
| Fix round | A fresh session that fixes a pull request after a failed check or review |
| Retro | The agent that finds the cause of a run's friction and may propose a change |

## Reference feature

A new project starts with one feature, the health endpoint, shaped as its own `ARCHITECTURE.md` says. These are its files as this repository keeps them, and `pnpm lint` fails when one names no file.

- **A route handler that only answers.** `.claude/skills/bootstrap/templates/apps/web/src/app/api/health/route.ts`
- **A module's door, deciding a rule.** `.claude/skills/bootstrap/templates/apps/web/src/domain/health/index.ts`
- **A unit test through the door.** `.claude/skills/bootstrap/templates/apps/web/src/domain/health/index.test.ts`
- **An end-to-end test.** `.claude/skills/bootstrap/templates/apps/web/e2e/smoke.spec.ts`

151	+
152	+- **Where it is.** Vercel sets `DATABASE_URL` on every deployment: production's database, or the preview's own branch. A local run has none.
153	+- **Tools.** Drizzle ORM over Neon's serverless driver in its HTTP mode (`drizzle-orm/neon-http`). Every query goes through `db()` in `src/db/client.ts`; nothing else in the app reads `DATABASE_URL` to connect.

155	+- **Add or change a table.** Edit `src/db/schema.ts`, run `pnpm db:generate --name <what-changes>` in `apps/web`, and commit the migration it writes to `src/db/migrations`: the SQL and Drizzle's record of the schema beside it. A table's queries go in the `repository.ts` of the module that owns it.
156	+- **How a migration reaches a preview and production.** `pnpm build` runs `src/db/migrate.mts` before it builds the app. The script applies every migration the deployment's database has not had, in order. Vercel runs that build for every deployment, so a pull request's migration runs on its preview's own database branch, and on production's database when the merge to `main` builds. A migration that fails fails the build, and the deployment before it keeps serving. With no `DATABASE_URL`, as on a local run or in CI's build, the script runs nothing.
157	+- **A migration merged out of order fails the build.** Drizzle's migrator skips, without saying so, a migration dated before the newest one the database has had. 718	+type OutboundInit = Omit<RequestInit, "signal"> & {
719	+  /** A shorter time limit for this call. One longer than the default is ignored. */
720	+  answerWithinMs?: number;
721	+};

723	+/**

725	+ * the time limit, or the call fails with an `OutboundError`. An answer with an error status is
726	+ * still an answer, and is the caller's to read.
727	+ */
728	+export async function outboundFetch(
729	+  url: string | URL,
730	+  { answerWithinMs = ANSWER_WITHIN_MS, ...init }: OutboundInit = {},
731	+): Promise<Response> {
732	+  const limit = Math.min(answerWithinMs, ANSWER_WITHIN_MS);
733	+  const giveUp = new AbortController();
734	+  const timer = setTimeout(() => giveUp.abort(), limit);

## Principles

- **One deployable.** A modular monolith: one Next.js app, one Postgres database. Split only when a measured problem demands it.

- **Simple for today's scale.** No queues, caches, or abstractions for load or variation we don't have.

## Structure

```
apps/web/src/
  domain/              what the product knows and does. No React and no Next.js.
    <module>/
      index.ts         the module's door: its use cases and types, nothing else
      types.ts         the module's entity, value objects, states and events
      state.ts         pure state transitions, where the module has a process
      <use-case>.ts    one use case in each file
      repository.ts    the only code that reads or writes the module's tables
      *.test.ts        tests of what the door promises
  components/          the design system. No product knowledge.
    ui/                shadcn's components, as shadcn ships them
  app/                 the web screens
    _components/       product components that two or more routes use, one in each file
    <route>/
      page.tsx         the page and nothing else
      actions.ts       server actions: read the session, call a use case
      _components/     this route's own components, one in each file
  lib/                 helpers with no product knowledge, each a folder: outbound/
  db/                  the database client, the schema and the migrations
```

- **Which folder may import which.** `app` imports `domain`, `components` and `lib`. `domain` imports `lib` and `db`, and another module only through that module's `index.ts`. `components`, `lib` and `db` import nothing above them. A client component imports from a module only its `types.ts` and `state.ts`. No file sits loose in `src/` but what Next.js requires there.
- **What a module is.** An entity: something the product stores, with an identity. A service: it works something out from entities and stores nothing. A source: it talks to an outside system and fills an entity.
- **Types are the contract.** A module's `types.ts` defines what it works with, and every exported function takes and returns those named types: no object type written inline, and no `ReturnType` of another module's function. An answer that can be one of several cases says which with a `status` field. A module answers real values, such as seconds or a ratio; formatting one is the screen's work.
- **Where state lives.** The highest of these that fits: the server, through a module; the address; one component; and a shared client store only when two unrelated components need state that lives nowhere above.
- **A process is a state machine in `domain`:** a state type and a pure transition function in `state.ts`, unit-tested, and a component that shows the state and sends it events.
- **Errors.** A failure the product expects is a value with a `status`. One it does not expect reaches the route's error boundary.
- **The test for where a rule goes:** were the web screens replaced by a mobile app, no rule would be lost.

## Modules

A module of `src/domain` is a deep module (`TASTE.md`). These rules shape one.

- **A module is one concept of the product.** Its `index.ts` is its only door, and its `repository.ts` alone reads and writes its tables. ESLint fails an import of any other file in its folder from outside it.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Scaffolds the monorepo in the current directory: a Next.js app with shadcn/ui on a closed
# grey-scale theme, the factory's own files (skills, workflows, ticket templates, check scripts,
# test tooling) and the seed docs.
# Then proves it lints, typechecks, passes the app's tests and builds.
# Safe to re-run: each part is skipped if it already exists.
# Usage: scaffold.sh [name]   (name defaults to the directory name)

name="${1:-$(basename "$PWD")}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
templates="$here/../templates"
manifest="$here/../manifest.txt"
factory_root="$(cd "$here/../../../.." && pwd)"   # the repo this skill lives in is the factory's source

    case "$path" in '' | '#'*) continue ;; esac
    # A file the factory owns inside the app comes from this repo where it holds the app, and from
    # the seeds where it holds none, as the repo the factory is published from does (decisions S420h).
    from="$factory_root"
    case "$path" in apps/*) [ -e "$factory_root/$path" ] || from="$templates" ;; esac
    if [ ! -e "$from/$path" ]; then
      # A listed folder under factory/ may hold nothing yet, and git keeps no empty folder:
      # factory/free-tier before the first ticket adds an entry. A mistyped path there is still
      # caught, because the file it meant is then one check-inventory.sh finds no owner for.
      # That check reads nothing outside factory/, so any other path that names nothing stops
      # the scaffold here: skipped, the new project would be built without the file.
      case "$path" in factory/*) continue ;; esac
      echo "scaffold: manifest.txt lists '$path', which is not in $from. Correct or remove the line." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    (cd "$from" && find "$path" -type f 2>/dev/null) | while IFS= read -r file; do
      # It proves the package tinyfactory publishes, which no project does (decisions W501).
      [ "$file" != factory/workflows/scaffold.yml ] || continue
      if [ "$mode" = overwrite ] || [ ! -e "$file" ]; then
        mkdir -p "$(dirname "$file")"
        cp "$from/$file" "$file"
      fi
    done
  done < "$manifest"
  # The workflows GitHub runs are copies of the sources just installed. They are made here and
  # not listed in the manifest, so each workflow lives once in the factory's repo and a new
  # project starts with the two folders matching, which its lint checks (check-inventory.sh).
  # Afterwards only install-workflows.yml changes them, once a change to a source merges.
  mkdir -p .github/workflows
  for file in factory/workflows/*; do
    if [ "$mode" = overwrite ] || [ ! -e ".github/workflows/$(basename "$file")" ]; then
      cp "$file" ".github/workflows/$(basename "$file")"
    fi
  done
}

fresh=no
if [ ! -d apps/web ]; then
  fresh=yes
  mkdir -p apps  # create-next-app refuses to run if the parent folder is missing

    --ts --eslint --app --src-dir --tailwind --import-alias "@/*" \
    --use-pnpm --skip-install --disable-git --yes

  # create-next-app assumes a standalone app; lift its workspace settings to the root.
  # The three folders after apps/* hold nothing to build or install: each is a package, by the
  # package.json the manifest gives it, so that Vercel builds nothing for a change inside one
  # (decisions M165a).
  {
    printf 'packages:\n  - apps/*\n  - factory\n  - .claude\n  - .github\n'
    if [ -f apps/web/pnpm-workspace.yaml ]; then echo; cat apps/web/pnpm-workspace.yaml; fi
  } > pnpm-workspace.yaml
  # The starter page is replaced by the factory's seed page, which uses the design tokens.
  rm -f apps/web/pnpm-workspace.yaml apps/web/README.md apps/web/src/app/page.tsx
  # create-next-app titles every page "Create Next App", which a visitor reads in the tab and in a shared link.
  python3 - "$name" apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx <<'PY'
import json, pathlib, sys
name, layout = sys.argv[1], pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2])
text = layout.read_text()
for old, new in (
    ('title: "Create Next App"', "title: " + json.dumps(name)),
    ('description: "Generated by create next app"', 'description: "Something new is taking shape here."'),
):
    assert text.count(old) == 1, f"create-next-app's `{old}` was not found in {layout}"

    cd apps/web
    npm pkg delete packageManager

    npm pkg set scripts.typecheck="next typegen && tsc --noEmit" \
      scripts.test="vitest run" scripts.test:e2e="playwright test"

if [ ! -f package.json ]; then
  # Read the version before the redirect below creates an empty package.json, which pnpm chokes on.

{

    "dev": "pnpm --filter web dev",
    "build": "pnpm -r build",
    "lint": "factory/scripts/check-inventory.sh && factory/scripts/check-decisions.sh && factory/scripts/check-free-tier.sh && factory/scripts/check-citations.sh && factory/scripts/check-rule-files.sh && factory/scripts/check-reference-feature.sh && factory/scripts/readme.sh > /dev/null && factory/scripts/check-factory.sh && pnpm -r lint",

    "test": "factory/scripts/test-factory.sh && pnpm -r test",
    "test:e2e": "pnpm --filter web test:e2e"

# seeds go only into an app this run made: a project may since have replaced them (decisions S590d).
(cd "$templates" && find . -type f | sed 's|^\./||') | while IFS= read -r seed; do
  case "$seed" in apps/*) [ "$fresh" = yes ] || continue ;; esac
  if [ ! -e "$seed" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$seed")"
    sed "s/{{name}}/$name/g" "$templates/$seed" > "$seed"
  fi
done

# The design foundation (DESIGN.md): shadcn/ui's components on its default grey-scale theme of
# named tokens, with Tailwind's own palette removed so no other colour exists. The factory makes
# no design choices of its own here; it takes shadcn's defaults and closes the door behind them.
design_foundation() {
  local css=apps/web/src/app/globals.css
  if [ ! -f apps/web/components.json ]; then
    (cd apps/web && pnpm dlx shadcn@latest init -d -y --no-monorepo --no-rtl \
      button input label card badge table </dev/null)
  fi
  # Each helper in src/lib is a folder (ARCHITECTURE.md, "Structure"). `@/lib/utils` names the
  # folder's index as it named the file, so nothing that imports it changes.
  if [ -f apps/web/src/lib/utils.ts ]; then
    mkdir -p apps/web/src/lib/utils
    mv apps/web/src/lib/utils.ts apps/web/src/lib/utils/index.ts
  fi
  grep -q -- '--color-\*: initial' "$css" && return 0
  python3 - "$css" apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx <<'PY'
import pathlib, sys
css = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); text = css.read_text()

assert text.count(marker) == 1, "shadcn's theme block was not found in globals.css"

   are the named tokens below (see DESIGN.md). A class like bg-blue-500 produces nothing and
   fails lint. Adding a colour means adding a token here, which is a design decision. */
@theme {
  --color-*: initial;
  --color-black: #000;
  --color-white: #fff;
}

""" + marker)
# The one change to shadcn's theme: the page is the palette's lightest grey, so white cards read
# as raised. It is a token, not a one-off colour (decisions D7).
page = ":root {\n  --background: oklch(1 0 0);\n"
assert text.count(page) == 1, "shadcn's light background token was not found in globals.css"
text = text.replace(page, ":root {\n  /* The page is the palette's lightest grey (neutral-50) so that white cards read as raised. */\n  --background: oklch(0.985 0 0);\n")
# shadcn 4.23 points --font-sans at itself; the app's font is the variable the layout defines.
if "--font-geist-sans" in pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2]).read_text():
    text = text.replace("--font-sans: var(--font-sans);", "--font-sans: var(--font-geist-sans);")
    text = text.replace("--font-heading: var(--font-sans);", "--font-heading: var(--font-geist-sans);")
css.write_text(text)

}

# A lint that passes shows no rule at work, so the rule that keeps a module behind its index.ts is
# shown failing, on a page file that breaks it (decisions S570).
prove_domain_import_rule() {
  local probe=apps/web/src/app/import-past-index.tsx output status=0
  printf 'import "@/domain/health/index.test";\n' > "$probe"
  output=$(pnpm lint 2>&1) || status=$?
  rm -f "$probe"
  if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "scaffold: pnpm lint passed a component that imports @/domain/health/index.test, a file inside a module's folder other than its index.ts. apps/web/eslint.config.mjs must fail that import." >&2

  pnpm --filter web add -D vitest @playwright/test "@types/node@^24" \
    eslint-plugin-better-tailwindcss @axe-core/playwright drizzle-kit
